title: Expert-aware refusal suppression: how brittle is MoE safety to targeted steering?

original_idea.body: Compare refusal-suppression brittleness of a small MoE vs a comparable dense model, and test whether steering only refusal-relevant experts is more efficient.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Architectural brittleness (MoE refusal concentrated in few experts) is a concrete medium-horizon weaponization concern.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Expert-targeted steering in MoE requires understanding routing/expert internals; intermediate ML fundamentals needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused MoE-vs-dense comparison but expert-targeting adds an architecture-specific workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open MoE models, no internal access; architectural safety comparison is externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Small MoE + dense inference; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Expert-aware refusal steering is published; the MoE-vs-dense brittleness comparison is a partly-open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Expert-aware refusal steering exists; whether MoE refusal is more brittle than dense at similar size is a partly-open comparison.
